edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 41,000,000, subject to mutually agreed adjustments for cash, debt, unpaid transaction expenses and normalized working capital. Before signing, the parties shall agree the definitions, accounting principles, working-capital target, illustrative calculation and completion-accounts dispute procedure, without double counting. The price shall be payable at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by the Seller in writing, except for the portion deposited into the agreed escrow under Section 3. Any diligence-related request to change the price requires the Seller’s express agreement and shall not confer a unilateral repricing right on the Buyer.

2. Closing. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve Closing within 30 days after signing definitive documentation. This is a target only and not an unconditional obligation to close. Closing shall be subject to required regulatory and corporate approvals, delivery of agreed closing documents, and satisfaction or permitted waiver of customary closing conditions expressly specified in the definitive documentation. Buyer’s diligence and internal investment approval shall be completed before signing definitive documentation unless the parties expressly agree otherwise. The proposed outside date is 60 days after signing. Either party may terminate if Closing has not occurred by that date, unless its own material breach caused the failure to close; the parties may extend that date by mutual written agreement.

3. Representations, Interim Covenants and Indemnification. Before signing, the parties shall agree a financial-statements schedule identifying each audited annual and unaudited interim statement, its date and period, and the applicable accounting standards. Subject to sufficiently detailed disclosure schedules delivered and agreed before signing, the Seller shall represent that those statements fairly present, in all material respects, the Company’s financial position and results for the relevant dates and periods in accordance with the identified accounting standards, consistently applied, subject, for unaudited statements, only to normal year-end adjustments that are not material individually or in the aggregate and the absence of footnotes. The definitive documentation shall include customary representations concerning the Seller’s authority and title to the Shares, capitalization, taxes, undisclosed liabilities and material contracts, with appropriate scope, materiality and knowledge qualifications and disclosed exceptions. Disclosures shall qualify other representations only where their relevance is reasonably apparent. Between signing and Closing, the Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course consistent with past practice and preserve its business in all material respects. Material actions outside the ordinary course, including dividends, equity issuances, material borrowings, material asset dispositions and entry into or termination of material contracts, shall require Buyer consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, subject to agreed exceptions for disclosed matters, legal requirements and emergencies. Buyer shall have reasonable access for transaction purposes, subject to confidentiality, privilege, applicable law and noninterference with operations. As a proposed indemnification framework, general representations shall survive for 12 months after Closing, with a deductible basket equal to 1% of the purchase price and aggregate liability capped at 10% of the purchase price. An escrow equal to 5% of the purchase price shall secure general representation claims and be released after 12 months, less amounts reasonably reserved for timely notified, unresolved claims. Fundamental representations, tax matters, covenant breaches and fraud shall have separately negotiated survival periods, remedies and limitations; no unlimited liability is agreed by this proposal. The definitive documentation shall address claim procedures, defense and settlement of third-party claims, mitigation, no double recovery and exclusive contractual remedies, subject to agreed exceptions.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the terms of this Agreement and nonpublic information received in connection with the transaction confidential, except for disclosures required by applicable law or regulation or made on a need-to-know basis for evaluating, financing or implementing the transaction to relevant affiliates and representatives, including professional advisers and financing sources, who are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality. Each party shall be responsible for its recipients’ compliance with this Section. Where legally permitted, a party making a legally required disclosure shall give the other party reasonable advance notice and disclose only what is required. No public announcement concerning this Agreement or the transaction shall be made without the other party’s prior written consent, except as required by applicable law or regulation.

receiver.requested_changes:
1. Price and adjustments: Counter at USD 37,000,000 for the Shares on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital, subject to diligence, Buyer approval and definitive documentation. Specify equity value as the agreed base price plus eligible cash, less debt and debt-like items and unpaid transaction expenses, plus or minus closing working capital against an agreed target. Define all categories to prevent double counting. Establish the target from trailing 12-month monthly balances, adjusted for seasonality and agreed nonrecurring items. Seller to deliver an estimated closing statement five business days before Closing; Buyer to deliver completion accounts within 90 days afterward; Seller to have 30 days to object, followed by a 30-day resolution period and referral of remaining accounting disputes to an independent accountant acting as expert. No unilateral pre-signing repricing right is requested; Buyer remains free not to sign if diligence or economics are unsatisfactory.
2. Financial information and diligence: Request audited financial statements for the three most recently completed fiscal years, the latest available interim statements and comparable prior-year periods, and monthly management accounts through the latest available month. Identify the accounting framework and provide audit reports, accounting policies, trial balances, cash reconciliations, receivables/payables aging, inventory reports, debt and debt-like schedules, tax returns and exposures, transaction expenses, and monthly working-capital detail for the last 24 months. Provide material contracts, customer/supplier concentration, litigation, compliance, employee/benefit, IP, cybersecurity and related-party materials, together with draft disclosure schedules and management access.
3. Closing: Accept the conditional 30-day target and a 60-day outside date, subject to a further 30-day extension at Buyer’s election where specified regulatory approvals alone remain outstanding and Buyer is otherwise ready to close. Include representation bring-down, material covenant compliance, no injunction, required approvals and agreed material third-party consents as conditions, with appropriately defined material-adverse-effect protection. No diligence or investment-approval condition after signing is proposed.
4. Representations and interim covenants: Retain the financial-statement standard, including the limitation on interim adjustments. Add appropriate representations covering compliance, litigation, employment and benefits, IP, data protection, assets and related-party arrangements. Avoid blanket knowledge or materiality qualifications; negotiate them representation by representation. Disclosure schedules must identify exceptions with sufficient detail, and later updates must not automatically cure breaches. Require prompt notice of material developments and no value leakage, with ordinary-course restrictions and narrowly defined exceptions.
5. Indemnification: Counter with 24-month general survival, a 0.5% tipping basket, a 20% general cap and a 10% escrow securing, but not constituting the exclusive source of recovery for, general claims. Release the general escrow at 24 months less reasonable reserves for timely claims. Fundamental representations should survive six years with a purchase-price cap; tax claims should survive until 60 days after the applicable limitation period expires. Covenant claims should survive for an appropriate period following required performance. Separately identified diligence risks require specific indemnities outside the general basket and cap. Preserve claims for fraud without contractual caps or exclusions, and equitable relief; negotiate the remaining exclusive-remedy provisions consistently with those exceptions.
6. Confidentiality: Retain the expanded permissions and protections, coordinated with any existing NDA, without expanding disclosure beyond legitimate transaction purposes.
